text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Parliament's constitutional committee plans not solve the dispute over the legal procedures for joining European monetary union, and instead will only present various options.
- An incentive money reward is planned for workers who find themselves jobs after being out of work for more than two years, the Labour Ministry says.
- A nightcap before sleep confuses body hormones and makes for restless sleep, a new medical dissertation shows.
- French investment bank Paribas says the Helsinki bourse's HEX index could rise to 3,300 points by year-end, and it expects Finnish listed companies' profits to grow this year by 23 percent.
- The Helsinki stock exchange is planning a new share list for the innovative, small and medium-sized growth companies, the bourse's deputy managing director Mika Bjorklund says.
- Sweden and even Australia would be better monetary union partners for Finland than core European countries, a Swedish study says.
- Finland's Green part is scheduled to elect a leader this weekend, and a close race is expected between MP Satu Hassi and incumbent chairman Tuija Brax.
- The Finnish forestry industry hopes to see timber sales picking up.
- The issue of EMU membership for Finland may cause the Green party to leave the goverment, party representatives say.
- Computer manufacturing alone is no longer profitable -- companies must sell total solutions, says CEO of British computer group ICL Keith Todd on a visit to Finland.
- Prices of previously occupied apartments have risen sharply this year.
- Former state labour mediator Jorma Reini asked Supreme Administrative Court to overturn his dismisal from office.

- Effects of abolishing shipping companies' tax-free sales should be investigated again, says Transport Minister Matti Aura, assuming however that the European Commission will not revise its decision to end such sales in 1999.
